title: A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes injectivity
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's construction (2026) of a finitely generated torsion-free group G_inj in which the rank-zero Bott class of an embedded torus subgroup Z^2 vanishes in K_0 of the reduced group C*-algebra, while an integral class of degree two detects the torus. The K-homology class of the torus Dirac operator, induced to G_inj, then has infinite order and reduced assembly image zero, so reduced Baum-Connes assembly is not rationally injective. The first lesson computes the assembly of the torus class from the lattice assembly isomorphism and the Mishchenko comparison and deduces the theorem. Lessons 2 to 8 build a labelled tower: the Heisenberg group and its laws, streams with coefficient pools and universal corrections, auxiliary incidences and the recovery of padded prefixes, expanding permutation tables chosen by a sequential law, and the pruning of coherent returns, short cycles and short bicycles. Lessons 9 to 11 attach Heisenberg voltages and matrix weights: compact Bott projections spread over sheared torus rectangles, the Fourier envelope and the product sampler, and polynomial avoidance with finite norm tests and centered moments. Lessons 12 to 15 define the graphical group by the closed walks of the voltage cover, embed the cover in its Cayley graph, choose disjoint domains in the sheets and prove torsion-freeness and the integral detector. Lessons 16 to 18 carry Bott profiles into the reduced group algebra by carriers and finite Cayley formulas, kill the Bott class by a parity swindle in a norm quotient, and pass to a finitely generated subgroup.
prerequisites: programme course Kasparov's KK-theory (KT-KK): lessons The Baum-Connes assembly map and the conjecture (Theorems A.4, A.7, A.8, A.9 and A.10, Lemmas A.7b, A.9a and A.10a, formulas (Q5) and (U8)), Homotopy, associativity, the index pairing and KK-equivalence (Proposition 5.1) and Dirac classes and the cotangent Dolbeault element (the flat torus)

programme course K-theory of C*-algebras (KT-OPK): lessons Idempotents, projections and their equivalences (Corollary 3.3), Nonunital algebras: unitization, relative classes and half-exactness (Theorem 1.1) and Commutative and noncommutative tori (Corollary 3.7)

programme course A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison-Kaplansky conjecture (kadison-kaplansky-projections): lessons Streams, slots and slot evaluations (Lemma 5.1), The mean incidence and its gap (Lemma 2.1), Separated bands and equivariant traces (Lemma 2.1), Torsion-freeness (Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2), Girth and centered moments (Lemmas 1.1 and 3.1) and From the cover band to the Cayley projection (Lemma 4.2)

programme course A projection of irrational trace and the Baum-Connes conjecture (irrational-trace-and-baum-connes): lesson Graphical presentations and coned diagrams (Section 3, the statements (VK) and (MAP))

programme course Van Kampen diagrams (van-kampen-diagrams): lessons Plane maps (Propositions 1.2, 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3) and Van Kampen's lemma (Definition 1.1, Theorems 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1), which prove the statements (VK) and (MAP)

open_obligations: Named statements used without proof in the course: (BG) the bar model of a group is a contractible free Delta-complex whose quotient is a K(G,1), functorial in G, and (CC) cellular cohomology computes singular cohomology (Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Example 1B.7, Theorems 1B.8 and 3.5), used in the lessons Cone chains, torsion-freeness and the integral detector and The reduced assembly map and the torus class; (LB) line bundles on CW complexes are classified by the first Chern class, naturally, and vector bundles on compact Hausdorff spaces are summands of trivial bundles (Hatcher, Vector Bundles and K-Theory, Propositions 1.4 and 3.10, Theorem 3.2); (IND) the index pairing of [E] - [1] with the Dirac class of the flat torus is plus or minus the degree of the line bundle E, with a sign fixed by the conventions (the torus case of the Atiyah-Singer index theorem for twisted Dirac operators; Baum and van Erp, arXiv:1604.03502, Theorem 1); (HS) the theorem of Hanke and Schick on maximal assembly (arXiv:0705.2578, Theorem 1.2), used only for a remark in the first lesson. The first assertion of Theorem 1.1 depends on (BG) and (CC); the infinite order of the torus class also uses (LB) and (IND); the vanishing of its reduced assembly image uses only results of the programme.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
